title: Release plan: runtime-1.19 TP stability (Dedicated-first canary + rollback criteria)
creator: Connor O'Brien
project: Multi-GPU (TP) stability fixes (Serving Runtime Performance — Kernel + Scheduling)
description:
Owner: Connor O'Brien (Releases)
Tech leads: Noah Patel (runtime), Hiro Tanaka (kernels), Sofia Ivanova (scheduling)
SRE DRI: Rafael Mendes
Support/CS: Owen Phillips / Rachel Kim

Context
We’ve had repeated Dedicated and high-throughput Hosted timeouts attributable to TP stalls (incl. Feb 17 Sev1). runtime-1.19 includes stability hardening (scheduler fairness/collective ordering, NCCL stream sync, watchdog + safe abort/drain, KV cache safety, improved surfacing + observability). This ticket defines the release gates, canary schedule, Dedicated-first sequencing, rollback criteria, and comms checklist.

Scope of release (runtime-1.19 TP stability changes)
- Scheduler guardrails to prevent collective starvation (ENG-4824, PR-21841)
- NCCL stream/event synchronization hardening (ENG-4825, PR-21853)
- TP watchdog timeout + safe abort/drain path (ENG-4826, PR-21860)
- TP heartbeat + stall reason codes + tracing enrichment (ENG-4823, PR-21834 + PR-21872)
- KV cache compaction safety in TP (ENG-4827, PR-21866)
- Load-shedding on TP stall signals (PR-21875)
- API-layer error surfacing for NCCL/abort semantics (PR-21912)
- Alert/dashboards updates (observability-pack PR-412)
- Perf-canary TP stress scenarios (perf-canary PR-188) + benchmark-lab repro harness (benchmark-lab PR-97)

Release goals (what “good” looks like)
1) Reduce TP-induced request hang/timeout rate on Dedicated A100/H100 clusters by >=80% vs runtime-1.18 baseline under peak load.
2) No Sev1/Sov2 incidents attributable to TP stalls during canary window.
3) Improve time-to-triage: on-call can classify stall as compute vs comms vs scheduler within 10 minutes using dashboard + structured logs.
4) Ensure watchdog/abort does not cause cascading failures (no restart storms, no elevated 5xx due to false positives).

Gating checks (must pass before first Dedicated canary)
A) Code / build gates
- All TP stability PRs merged behind intended flags and included in runtime-1.19 release branch.
- CI: GPU integration tests green (including fault injection tests from PR-21905 when landed).
- Config defaults reviewed (no silent behavior changes in Hosted unless explicitly intended).

B) Functional + reliability gates (pre-canary)
- Repro harness (benchmark-lab PR-97) can deterministically trigger prior hang signature on runtime-1.18 and no longer hangs on runtime-1.19 for >=10 consecutive runs.
- Perf-canary TP stress suite (ENG-4828 / perf-canary PR-188):
  - Long context + bursty concurrency scenario: no hard hangs; watchdog triggers (if enabled) produce controlled abort + drain and do not wedge nodes.
  - p99 latency regression <= 5% vs baseline for “steady-state decode” scenario with stream sync hardening enabled.
  - Throughput regression <= 3% for median traffic mix (prefill/decode mixed) OR documented justification + mitigation (toggle/conditional sync).

C) Observability / on-call readiness gates
- Dashboard panels merged + deployed (observability-pack PR-412) and reviewed with SRE (Aisha Bello / Sergio Costa).
- Alerts configured but set to “ticket only” for first 24h of canary (no paging) unless we see real stalls.
- Runbook updated and linked in alert annotations (Confluence: runtime-tp-hang-mitigation + tp-stall-triage-playbook).
- Support-facing workaround doc updated with new version/flag guidance (Confluence CS/Support known issues page).

Feature flags / rollout knobs (must be explicitly tracked)
- tp_watchdog_enabled (default OFF in Hosted; ON for Dedicated canary only)
- tp_watchdog_timeout_ms (model-size tiered defaults; start conservative to avoid false positives)
- tp_nccl_sync_hardening_enabled (start ON in canary; ability to disable if perf regression)
- tp_scheduler_collective_fairness_enabled (ON; should be safe/correctness improvement)
- tp_stall_load_shed_enabled (ON in canary after first 24h if signals are stable)

Canary schedule (Dedicated-first)
Phase 0: Internal validation (T-3 to T-1 days)
- Run benchmark-lab repro + perf-canary TP scenarios on A100-80GB and H100 test clusters.
- Confirm dashboards/alerts show expected signals (heartbeat, in-flight collective counters, stall reason tags).
- Create a “canary war-room” Slack thread in #eng-releases and add DRIs.

Phase 1: Dedicated canary (Day 0–2)
- Select 1–2 Dedicated accounts with known TP timeout history + willingness to canary (target: Acme AI if aligned via PM-911 / CS).
- Roll 10% of replicas in the selected Dedicated clusters to runtime-1.19.
- Enable watchdog + extra NCCL logging for a bounded 4–6 hour window if approved (coordinate with INT-2219; ensure log sampling + redaction policy).
- Monitor: request timeouts, TP heartbeat gaps, drain events, NCCL errors, p99 latency, GPU utilization anomalies.

Phase 2: Dedicated expansion (Day 2–4)
- Increase to 50% replicas for canary accounts if no rollback triggers.
- Extend to 2–3 additional Dedicated clusters (mix of A100 and H100) with moderate traffic.
- Turn on tp_stall_load_shed_enabled after 24h if false positive rate is acceptable.

Phase 3: Dedicated full rollout (Day 4–7)
- Roll 100% replicas for Dedicated clusters (staged by region).
- Keep alerts “paging” enabled for SRE once confidence is high (after 48h at >=50% rollout with no major issues).

Phase 4: Hosted rollout (post-Dedicated success)
- Roll to Hosted canary clusters (lowest-risk region first).
- Watch for changes in streaming timeout rates and cancellation-path behavior (PR-21890).
- Gradually expand to all Hosted regions.

Rollback criteria (hard stop)
Immediate rollback to runtime-1.18 or disable flags if any occur during canary:
- Any repeatable hang where replicas wedge and do not recover via drain within 10 minutes.
- Increase in customer-visible 5xx or timeout rate by >0.5% absolute for canary accounts over 60 minutes, attributable to runtime behavior.
- Watchdog false positives: drain/restart events >3 per hour per cluster without corresponding request timeout reduction.
- p99 latency regression >10% sustained for >2 hours vs baseline, not explained by traffic mix changes.
- NCCL error rate spikes correlated with sync hardening changes (and not present in baseline).

Rollback actions (order of operations)
1) Disable tp_watchdog_enabled (fast mitigation if false positives/drain storms).
2) Disable tp_nccl_sync_hardening_enabled if perf regression / unexpected NCCL behavior.
3) Reduce TP concurrency caps (temporary mitigation; see known issues/workarounds doc).
4) Roll back runtime image to runtime-1.18 for impacted cluster(s).
5) If node-level wedging occurs: drain node pool, recycle GPUs; engage SRE incident process.

Comms checklist
Before Dedicated canary (T-24h)
- Notify SRE on-call + SRE leadership (Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes) with:
  - rollout window
  - flags to be enabled
  - dashboards + runbook links
  - rollback triggers
- Notify Support escalation lead (Owen Phillips): what errors may surface, expected customer-visible changes, how to route tickets.
- Notify PM (Paula Mendes / Lauren Bishop): which accounts, messaging, and who approves enabling extra logging.

During canary
- Update #eng-releases thread at least 2x/day with status + key metrics.
- If any rollback trigger is met: call it explicitly, execute rollback, and open incident channel if customer impact.

After canary
- Post canary readout (Dedicated metrics, issues found, final go/no-go for Hosted).
- Update known-issues page with resolved versions and remaining mitigations.

Links
- Linear initiative: ENG-4821
- Support/customer impact: PM-911
- PRs: PR-21834, PR-21841, PR-21853, PR-21860, PR-21866, PR-21872, PR-21875, PR-21912, observability-pack PR-412, perf-canary PR-188, benchmark-lab PR-97
- Confluence: ADR-0127 (watchdog/abort semantics), TP known issues, TP triage playbook, runtime TP hang mitigation runbook

Acceptance criteria
- Dedicated canary completes through Phase 2 (>=50% replicas) with no rollback triggers and with measured reduction in TP timeouts/hangs.
- SRE signs off that alerting + runbook coverage is sufficient for full rollout.
- PM/Support confirm comms ready for Dedicated accounts and Hosted rollout sequencing.

Open questions
- Final default watchdog thresholds by model tier (align with #eng-runtime thread on default values).
- Whether tp_nccl_sync_hardening_enabled should be unconditional or conditional on graph capture / model architecture.
- Hosted default behavior: keep watchdog OFF by default until at least one full release cycle of Dedicated data?
